blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Evaluation Record** in *Closed-Loop Evaluation* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Closed-Loop Evaluation, § The Evaluation Record
blocks.md: When a twenty-run door campaign finishes with twenty clean latches, the pass count alone cannot tell an auditor which strike-plate cell was tested, whether aborted runs were dropped from the denominator, or which network weights were loaded on the robot. The **evaluation record**, the fifth link in the record chain, preserves the formal reasoning that connects empirical observations to a bounded operational claim. It consumes the policy manifest, citing it by cryptographic digest, and incorporates the known absences listed in the provenance record of a later section.

questions.q: The section **The Evaluation Record** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: At zero failures the Wald interval collapses, so a clean record is inverted exactly (failure bound about 3/n), which makes twenty clean runs consistent with a one-in-seven failure rate and makes every added nine cost about ten times the trials.

The evaluation record binds a bounded claim to its target ODD, configuration digests, sampling protocol, complete outcome log, exact statistics, and the catalog of unsupported gaps, which become runtime obligations.
Coverage gaps the record cannot close become five runtime monitor channels (input support, latency and freshness, constraint margin, intervention rate, environmental assumption).
A simulator earns authority to screen candidates only through a paired sim-and-real benchmark scored for rank inversions, and even then it filters, never certifies.
